introduction: On this Sunday, Ezra reads the Law to all the people, who weep and then rejoice. In the Gospel, Saint Luke tells us why he wrote his account, and Jesus reads from Isaiah in the synagogue of Nazareth and says, Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing. Paul teaches that we are one body with many members. Let us welcome God's word as it is fulfilled among us today.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Spirit of the Lord anointed Jesus to bring good news to the poor. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church, the Body of Christ: that every member may be valued and no one left out. Let us pray to the Lord.
For readers and all who proclaim God's word: that they may proclaim it clearly and with faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor, prisoners, the blind and the oppressed: that they may hear the good news of liberty. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who suffer: that the whole body of the Church may suffer with them and support them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that God's word may be fulfilled in our lives today. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son was anointed by the Spirit to bring good news to the poor. Open our ears to your word and make us one body in him, serving the needs of all. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Today this Scripture is fulfilled
reflection.body:
After the exile, the people gather in Jerusalem, and Ezra reads the book of the Law to them "from early morning until midday." They listen attentively, and when they understand, they weep. But the leaders tell them, "Today is holy to the LORD your God. Don't mourn, nor weep." And they add, "the joy of the LORD is your strength." Hearing God's word is meant to lead to joy and to sharing with those who have nothing.

Luke begins his Gospel by telling his friend Theophilus why he wrote: so "that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed." The Gospel is not a legend but a careful account of real events, handed down from eyewitnesses.

Then Luke takes us to Nazareth. Jesus goes to the synagogue on the Sabbath, "as was his custom," and reads from Isaiah: "The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor." He rolls up the scroll and sits down, and everyone's eyes are fixed on him. Then he says, "Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing." This is the program of his whole mission: good news for the poor, freedom for captives, sight for the blind.

Paul tells us how Christ's mission continues: through his body, the Church. "Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually." No member can say to another, "I have no need for you." And "When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it."

This week, read a passage of Luke's Gospel each day and listen as if Jesus were speaking to you today. And think of one member of the body who is suffering, and find a way to share their burden.
